name: gmail_watch
description: Runs automatically every 2 hours to check Gmail, summarize what's new, and ALWAYS speak up when something is important or time-sensitive; silent only when everything is routine.
instructions: Use the mcp_gmail tools to check for unread/new email. Summarize it in a couple of sentences. Judge whether anything is genuinely important or time-sensitive: a real person (personal message) needing a reply, a deadline, a security/account alert (new sign-in, password reset, suspicious activity), a payment/billing problem, or anything urgent - versus routine newsletters/promos/automated notifications. Always call remember_fact (category="fact") with a one-line record of this check, e.g. "Gmail check <time>: N unread, nothing important" or "...: important - <what>", so there's a saved log either way. Then decide the final reply, and this rule is mandatory: if your summary identifies ANY important or time-sensitive email, your final reply MUST be a short spoken alert naming who it is from and what it is about (one to three sentences) - never leave the reply empty in that case, and never save the finding only to memory. Only if everything is routine or unimportant, give NO spoken reply at all - respond with empty text, since this is a silent background check. When unsure whether something is important, lean towards speaking.
